script.title: ABC vs Traditional Costing
script.caption_hook: Why do simple and complex products pay the same rate per hour?

lines.say: Why do simple and complex products pay the same rate per hour?
Traditional costing shares overhead by volume, like labour hours. ABC shares it by the activities each product uses.
So like splitting a restaurant bill?
Restaurant bill, yes. Traditional splits by total food eaten. ABC charges only for dishes ordered.
Overhead is ₹60,000. A uses 500 labour hours, B uses 100. Rate is ₹60,000 divided by 600, so ₹100 per hour.
So A pays ₹50,000 and B pays ₹10,000?
Yes. But B needs four set-ups, A only two. B causes more cost.
Then how does ABC fix that?
Say all overhead is set-up cost. A has two set-ups, B has four. That's six, so ₹10,000 per set-up.
Yes. Total stays ₹60,000. Only the sharing changes.
So ABC doesn't reduce total cost?
Correct. Cost falls only if management acts on that information, like dropping activities that add no value.
